note: The header type declares five fields and the body carries six: c0 07 06 is list8 with size 7 and count 6, then six nulls. A reader that accepted a longer list would be reading a field the declared surface does not have, and the extra value would be silently dropped. Reading: Part 3 states the field set and names no condition for a body that exceeds it, so the refusal is amqp:decode-error, the pinned shared condition whose definition (data could not be decoded) fits.

durable is field 1 of header and its declared type is boolean; a1 01 78 is the string x. A reader that ignored declared types would admit it and a later consumer would find a string where the artifact promises a boolean. Reading: amqp:decode-error, as for the structural refusals.

received declares section-number and section-offset both mandatory. The body carries one item, 70 00000005 (uint 5), so the mandatory prefix is short: a decoder that stopped at the first missing field would produce a received state with no offset, and the resume point would be wrong in the direction that loses data. Reading: amqp:decode-error.

data restricts binary, so its body must be a variable-width octet string; 45 is list0, a compound. The section name says binary and the body says list, and a reader that dispatched only on the descriptor would read the wrong shape. Reading: amqp:decode-error.
footer restricts annotations, which restricts map: its body is a map of pairs and never a field list. 45 is list0. Reading: amqp:decode-error.

a1 02 6869 is a perfectly well-formed string, and every section is a described type: the section's type is named by a descriptor, so a bare value is not a section at all. This is the vector that separates 'the octets decoded' from 'the octets are a section'. Reading: amqp:decode-error.

00 53 ff is a descriptor whose ulong is 255, which no declared type carries. An endpoint that accepted it would be receiving a section type the specification does not define. Reading: amqp:decode-error; the artifact's list of sections is closed for message format 0, so an undeclared descriptor is refused rather than passed through.

00 53 10 is a described value whose descriptor is a declared type that provides no section role: open, the transport performative. The descriptor resolves, so this is the vector that pins the section role rather than the descriptor table. Reading: amqp:decode-error.

The list8 announces two elements in four octets and the octets stop one short: 00 53 70 c0 04 02 41 ends after the boolean. A reader that returned what it had would hand its caller a header whose second field is missing rather than absent. The reason class is truncated, not malformed: nothing here contradicts the declared shape, the octets simply stop.
The annotations text restricts the keys to symbol or ulong, and 40 is null; the map is c1 03 02 40 41, one pair whose key is null. Reading: amqp:decode-error.

application-properties restricts the keys to strings, unlike the three annotations-sourced sections whose keys are symbols or ulongs. 53 01 is a smallulong key and a1 01 78 a string value, so the section is well formed as a map and wrong as an application-properties. Reading: amqp:decode-error.

application-properties restricts the values to simple types, excluding map, list and array. The pair is a string key a1 01 6b and a list value 45: c1 05 02 a1 01 6b 45. This is the section's own value restriction rather than a map-key rule, so it is refused even though the map itself is well formed. Reading: amqp:decode-error.

The same octets as sec-message-annotations-decode-understood-ulong-key, with the endpoint's policy empty: 53 01 is a reserved ulong key the receiver does not implement, it does not begin with x-opt, and the clause mandates a detach for exactly that. The pair of vectors is the isolation the negative-vector rule asks for: disabling the key rule makes this vector stop failing for this reason, and the positive twin differs only in the policy.

The artifact states one value rule for annotations and names the key: any value associated with the reserved symbolic key rejected MUST be of type error. The policy names rejected so the key is understood, and the value is a1 01 78, a string. This vector is clause-backed end to end: the key rule is a MUST, the type is named, and the refusal is not a reading. Reading for the condition itself: amqp:decode-error.

The same map as sec-footer-decode-symbol-key-null-value with the key it had before the fix: a3 01 6b is the symbol k, which is neither an x-opt key nor one the empty policy implements, so the clause's mandated detach applies. c1 05 02 sizes the map. The pair of vectors is rule-isolated: the octets differ only in the key, and disabling the key rule makes this vector stop failing for this reason.
